import Foundation.FirstOrder.Completeness.Coding
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Order

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

namespace Completeness

open Semiformula Encodable System
variable {L : Language.{u}}
variable {T : Theory L} {Γ : Sequent L}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺[" c:25 "] " Δ₂:80 => Redux T c Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma Redux.antimonotone {c : Code L} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h <;> simp[List.subset_cons_of_subset _ (List.subset_cons_self _ _)]

variable [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Func k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Rel k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Func k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Rel k)]

inductive ReduxNat (T : Theory L) (s : ℕ) : Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | redux {c : Code L} : decode s.unpair.1 = some c → ∀ {Δ₂ Δ₁}, Redux T c Δ₂ Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁
  | refl : decode (α := Code L) s.unpair.1 = none → ∀ Δ, ReduxNat T s Δ Δ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺⟨" s:25 "⟩ " Δ₂:80 => ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma ReduxNat.antimonotone {s : ℕ} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨s⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h; { exact Redux.antimonotone (by assumption) }; { exact List.Subset.refl Δ₂ }

lemma ReduxNat.toRedux {c : Code L} {i} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨(encode c).pair i⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁ := by
  rcases h with (⟨h, r⟩ | ⟨h⟩); { simp at h; simpa[h] using r }; { simp at h }

inductive SearchTreeAux (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : ℕ → Sequent L → Type u
  | zero : SearchTreeAux T Γ 0 Γ
  | succ : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁ → SearchTreeAux T Γ (s + 1) Δ₂

def SearchTree (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) := (s : ℕ) × (Δ : Sequent L) × SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ

namespace SearchTree

abbrev rank (τ : SearchTree T Γ) := τ.1

abbrev seq (τ : SearchTree T Γ) := τ.2.1

inductive Lt (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : SearchTree T Γ → SearchTree T Γ → Prop
  | intro {s} {Δ₂ Δ₁} (a : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁) (r : ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁) : Lt T Γ ⟨s + 1, Δ₂, a.succ r⟩ ⟨s, Δ₁, a⟩

lemma rank_of_lt {τ₁ τ₂ : SearchTree T Γ} (h : Lt T Γ τ₂ τ₁) : τ₂.rank = τ₁.rank + 1 := by
  cases h; simp

lemma seq_of_lt {τ₁ τ₂ : SearchTree T Γ} (h : Lt T Γ τ₂ τ₁) : τ₂.seq ≺⟨τ₁.rank⟩ τ₁.seq := by
  cases h; simp[rank, seq]; assumption

instance : Top (SearchTree T Γ) := ⟨⟨0, Γ, SearchTreeAux.zero⟩⟩

@[simp] lemma rank_top : (⊤ : SearchTree T Γ).rank = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma seq_top : (⊤ : SearchTree T Γ).seq = Γ := rfl

end SearchTree

section WellFounded

variable (wf : WellFounded (SearchTree.Lt T Γ))

noncomputable def SearchTree.recursion {C : SearchTree T Γ → Sort v}
  (τ) (h : ∀ τ₁, (∀ τ₂, SearchTree.Lt T Γ τ₂ τ₁ → C τ₂) → C τ₁) : C τ :=
  WellFounded.fix wf h τ

noncomputable def syntacticMainLemma (φ : SearchTree T Γ) : T ⟹ φ.seq := by
  apply SearchTree.recursion wf φ
  intro ⟨s, Δ₁, a₁⟩ ih
  have ih' : ∀ {Δ₂}, ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁ → T ⟹ Δ₂ := fun {Δ₂} r => ih ⟨s + 1, Δ₂, a₁.succ r⟩ (SearchTree.Lt.intro a₁ r)
  rcases hs : (decode s.unpair.1 : Option (Code L)) with (_ | c)
  · have : ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₁ := ReduxNat.refl hs Δ₁
    exact ih' this
  · cases c
    case axL r v =>
      by_cases hr : rel r v ∈ Δ₁ ∧ nrel r v ∈ Δ₁
      · exact Tait.em hr.1 hr.2
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.axLRefl r v (not_and_or.mp hr))
    case verum =>
      by_cases h : ⊤ ∈ Δ₁
      · exact Tait.verum' h
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.verumRefl h)
    case and φ ψ =>
      by_cases h : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Δ₁
      · have rp : φ :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.and φ ψ] Δ₁ := Redux.and₁ h
        have rq : ψ :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.and φ ψ] Δ₁ := Redux.and₂ h
        have dp : T ⟹ φ :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs rp)
        have dq : T ⟹ ψ :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs rq)
        exact Tait.wk (Tait.and dp dq) (by simpa using h)
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.andRefl h)
    case or φ ψ =>
      by_cases h : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Δ₁
      · have : φ :: ψ :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.or φ ψ] Δ₁ := Redux.or h
        have : T ⟹ φ :: ψ :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs this)
        exact Tait.wk (Tait.or this) (by simpa using h)
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.orRefl h)
    case all φ =>
      by_cases h : ∀' φ ∈ Δ₁
      · have : φ/[&(newVar Δ₁)] :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.all φ] Δ₁ := Redux.all h
        have : T ⟹ φ/[&(newVar Δ₁)] :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs this)
        exact Derivation.allNvar h this
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.allRefl h)
    case ex φ t =>
      by_cases h : ∃' φ ∈ Δ₁
      · have : φ/[t] :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.ex φ t] Δ₁ := Redux.ex h
        have : T ⟹ φ/[t] :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs this)
        exact Tait.wk (Derivation.ex t this) (by simpa using h)
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.exRefl h)
    case id φ =>
      by_cases h : φ ∈ T
      · have : (∼∀∀φ) :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.id φ] Δ₁ := Redux.id h
        have : T ⟹ (∼∀∀φ) :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs this)
        exact Derivation.id h this
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.idRefl h)

noncomputable def syntacticMainLemmaTop : T ⟹ Γ := by exact?

noncomputable def syntacticMainLemma (φ : SearchTree T Γ) : T ⟹ φ.seq := by
  apply SearchTree.recursion wf φ
  intro ⟨s, Δ₁, a₁⟩ ih
  have ih' : ∀ {Δ₂}, ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁ → T ⟹ Δ₂ := fun {Δ₂} r => ih ⟨s + 1, Δ₂, a₁.succ r⟩ (SearchTree.Lt.intro a₁ r)
  rcases hs : (decode s.unpair.1 : Option (Code L)) with (_ | c)
  · have : ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₁ := ReduxNat.refl hs Δ₁
    exact ih' this
  · cases c
    case axL r v =>
      by_cases hr : rel r v ∈ Δ₁ ∧ nrel r v ∈ Δ₁
      · exact Tait.em hr.1 hr.2
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.axLRefl r v (not_and_or.mp hr))
    case verum =>
      by_cases h : ⊤ ∈ Δ₁
      · exact Tait.verum' h
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.verumRefl h)
    case and φ ψ =>
      by_cases h : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Δ₁
      · have rp : φ :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.and φ ψ] Δ₁ := Redux.and₁ h
        have rq : ψ :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.and φ ψ] Δ₁ := Redux.and₂ h
        have dp : T ⟹ φ :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs rp)
        have dq : T ⟹ ψ :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs rq)
        exact Tait.wk (Tait.and dp dq) (by simpa using h)
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.andRefl h)
    case or φ ψ =>
      by_cases h : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Δ₁
      · have : φ :: ψ :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.or φ ψ] Δ₁ := Redux.or h
        have : T ⟹ φ :: ψ :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs this)
        exact Tait.wk (Tait.or this) (by simpa using h)
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.orRefl h)
    case all φ =>
      by_cases h : ∀' φ ∈ Δ₁
      · have : φ/[&(newVar Δ₁)] :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.all φ] Δ₁ := Redux.all h
        have : T ⟹ φ/[&(newVar Δ₁)] :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs this)
        exact Derivation.allNvar h this
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.allRefl h)
    case ex φ t =>
      by_cases h : ∃' φ ∈ Δ₁
      · have : φ/[t] :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.ex φ t] Δ₁ := Redux.ex h
        have : T ⟹ φ/[t] :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs this)
        exact Tait.wk (Derivation.ex t this) (by simpa using h)
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.exRefl h)
    case id φ =>
      by_cases h : φ ∈ T
      · have : (∼∀∀φ) :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.id φ] Δ₁ := Redux.id h
        have : T ⟹ (∼∀∀φ) :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs this)
        exact Derivation.id h this
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.idRefl h)

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.eval_close
rag.content:
lemma eval_close {ε} (φ : SyntacticFormula L) :
    Evalf s ε (∀∀φ) ↔ ∀ f, Evalf s f φ := by
  simp [close, eval_rew, Function.comp_def, Matrix.empty_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h f
    refine (eval_iff_of_funEqOn φ ?_).mp (h (fun x ↦ f x))
    intro x hx; simp [Rew.fixitr_fvar, lt_fvSup_of_fvar? hx]
  · intro h f
    refine (eval_iff_of_funEqOn φ ?_).mp (h (fun x ↦ if hx : x < φ.fvSup then f ⟨x, by simp [hx]⟩ else ε 0))
    intro x hx; simp [Rew.fixitr_fvar, lt_fvSup_of_fvar? hx]

    T ⊨[Struc.{v, u} L] φ ↔ (∀ (M : Type v) [Nonempty M] [Structure L M] [M ⊧ₘ* T], M ⊧ₘ φ) :=
  ⟨fun h _ _ s _ => Semantics.consequence_iff'.mp h s.toStruc,
   fun h s hs => @h s.Dom s.nonempty s.struc hs⟩

rag.content:
def Eval (s : Structure L M) (e : Fin n → M) (ε : ξ → M) : Semiformula L ξ n →ˡᶜ Prop where
  toTr := EvalAux s ε e
  map_top' := rfl
  map_bot' := rfl
  map_and' := by simp [EvalAux]
  map_or' := by simp [EvalAux]
  map_neg' := by simp [EvalAux_neg]
  map_imply' := by simp [imp_eq, EvalAux_neg, ←neg_eq, EvalAux, imp_iff_not_or]

abbrev Evalm (M : Type w) [s : Structure L M] {n} (e : Fin n → M) (ε : ξ → M) :
    Semiformula L ξ n →ˡᶜ Prop := Eval s e ε

informal_statement: If the tree structure with the given properties is not well-founded, then the model satisfies the formula T in the bounded semantics.
informal_proof:
To establish that the model \( Model(T, \Gamma) \) satisfies \( T \) in the bounded semantics \( \models_{m}^{*} \), we proceed as follows:

1. **Assumption of the Model**: We start with the premise that the model \( Model(T, \Gamma) \) is constructed such that it adheres to the bounded semantics \( \models_{m}^{*} \). This semantics typically restricts satisfaction to finite or bounded paths or structures within the model.

2. **Contextual Background**: In the context of Lean4's formal system, \( Model(T, \Gamma) \) represents an interpretation where clauses or formulas are evaluated within a certain structure defined by \( T \) and \( \Gamma \). The operator \( \models_{m}^{*} \) signifies that the formula \( T \) evaluates to true or holds under this bounded interpretation.

3. **Role of `Semiformula.eval_close`**: The Lean4 function `Semiformula.eval_close` is used to evaluate a closed formula within this model. A closed formula is one that contains no free variables, allowing for direct evaluation without variable substitution. This function `eval_close` is crucial as it ensures that the evaluation respects the model's structure and the boundedness imposed by \( \models_{m}^{*} \).

4. **Contrapositive Approach**: Assuming that \( Model(T, \Gamma) \not\models_{m}^{*} T \) leads to a contradiction in the structure of the model. Specifically, if the formula \( T \) fails to evaluate to true in the bounded semantics, it implies the existence of a well-founded tree structure within \( T \) and \( \Gamma \) that violates the conditions imposed by the model's boundedness.

5. **Contradiction and Conclusion**: The assumption leads to the situation where we have both a model of \( T \) and a well-founded tree structure incompatible with the model's bounded semantics. This contradiction necessitates that our initial assumption is false, thereby confirming that \( Model(T, \Gamma) \models_{m}^{*} T \).

6. **Conclusion**: Therefore, under the absence of a well-founded tree structure that would conflict with the bounded semantics, the formula \( T \) must indeed hold in \( Model(T, \Gamma) \) under \( \models_{m}^{*} \).

This completes the proof, establishing that \( Model(T, \Gamma) \models_{m}^{*} T \) when the tree structure is not well-founded, aligning with the bounded semantics defined in the model.

      ih : (τ₂ : LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.SearchTree T Γ) → LO.FirstOrder.Complete …
      ih' : {Δ₂ : LO.FirstOrder.Sequent L} → LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.ReduxNat T s …
      hs : Eq (Encodable.decode (Nat.unpair s).1) Option.none
      ⊢ LO.OneSided.Derivation T (LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.SearchTree.seq ⟨s, ⟨Δ₁, …
    -/
  · have : ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₁ := ReduxNat.refl hs Δ₁
    /-
      case none
      L : LO.FirstOrder.Language
      T : LO.FirstOrder.Theory L
      Γ : LO.FirstOrder.Sequent L
      inst✝³ : (k : Nat) → DecidableEq (L.Func k)
      inst✝² : (k : Nat) → DecidableEq (L.Rel k)
      inst✝¹ : (k : Nat) → Encodable (L.Func k)
      inst✝ : (k : Nat) → Encodable (L.Rel k)
      wf : WellFounded (LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.SearchTree.Lt T Γ)
      φ : LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.SearchTree T Γ
      s : Nat
      Δ₁ : LO.FirstOrder.Sequent L
      a₁ : LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁
      ih : (τ₂ : LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.SearchTree T Γ) → LO.FirstOrder.Complete …
      ih' : {Δ₂ : LO.FirstOrder.Sequent L} → LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.ReduxNat T s …
      hs : Eq (Encodable.decode (Nat.unpair s).1) Option.none
      this : LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₁
      ⊢ LO.OneSided.Derivation T (LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.SearchTree.seq ⟨s, ⟨Δ₁, …
    -/
    exact ih' this
    /-
      🎉 no goals
    -/
    /-
      case some
      L : LO.FirstOrder.Language
      T : LO.FirstOrder.Theory L
      Γ : LO.FirstOrder.Sequent L
      inst✝³ : (k : Nat) → DecidableEq (L.Func k)
      inst✝² : (k : Nat) → DecidableEq (L.Rel k)
      inst✝¹ : (k : Nat) → Encodable (L.Func k)
      inst✝ : (k : Nat) → Encodable (L.Rel k)
      wf : WellFounded (LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.SearchTree.Lt T Γ)
      φ : LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.SearchTree T Γ
      s : Nat
      Δ₁ : LO.FirstOrder.Sequent L
      a₁ : LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁
      ih : (τ₂ : LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.SearchTree T Γ) → LO.FirstOrder.Complete …
      ih' : {Δ₂ : LO.FirstOrder.Sequent L} → LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.ReduxNat T s …
      c : LO.FirstOrder.System.Code L
      hs : Eq (Encodable.decode (Nat.unpair s).1) (Option.some c)
      ⊢ LO.OneSided.Derivation T (LO.FirstOrder.Completeness.SearchTree.seq ⟨s, ⟨Δ₁, …
    -/
  · cases c
    case axL r v =>
      by_cases hr : rel r v ∈ Δ₁ ∧ nrel r v ∈ Δ₁
      · exact Tait.em hr.1 hr.2
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.axLRefl r v (not_and_or.mp hr))
    case verum =>
      by_cases h : ⊤ ∈ Δ₁
      · exact Tait.verum' h
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.verumRefl h)
    case and φ ψ =>
      by_cases h : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Δ₁
      · have rp : φ :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.and φ ψ] Δ₁ := Redux.and₁ h
        have rq : ψ :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.and φ ψ] Δ₁ := Redux.and₂ h
        have dp : T ⟹ φ :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs rp)
        have dq : T ⟹ ψ :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs rq)
        exact Tait.wk (Tait.and dp dq) (by simpa using h)
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.andRefl h)
    case or φ ψ =>
      by_cases h : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Δ₁
      · have : φ :: ψ :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.or φ ψ] Δ₁ := Redux.or h
        have : T ⟹ φ :: ψ :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs this)
        exact Tait.wk (Tait.or this) (by simpa using h)
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.orRefl h)
    case all φ =>
      by_cases h : ∀' φ ∈ Δ₁
      · have : φ/[&(newVar Δ₁)] :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.all φ] Δ₁ := Redux.all h
        have : T ⟹ φ/[&(newVar Δ₁)] :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs this)
        exact Derivation.allNvar h this
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.allRefl h)
    case ex φ t =>
      by_cases h : ∃' φ ∈ Δ₁
      · have : φ/[t] :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.ex φ t] Δ₁ := Redux.ex h
        have : T ⟹ φ/[t] :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs this)
        exact Tait.wk (Derivation.ex t this) (by simpa using h)
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.exRefl h)
    case id φ =>
      by_cases h : φ ∈ T
      · have : (∼∀∀φ) :: Δ₁ ≺[Code.id φ] Δ₁ := Redux.id h
        have : T ⟹ (∼∀∀φ) :: Δ₁ := ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs this)
        exact Derivation.id h this
      · exact ih' (ReduxNat.redux hs $ Redux.idRefl h)

C1_dependencies.name: id
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
The identity function. `id` takes an implicit argument `α : Sort u`
(a type in any universe), and an argument `a : α`, and returns `a`.

Although this may look like a useless function, one application of the identity
function is to explicitly put a type on an expression. If `e` has type `T`,
and `T'` is definitionally equal to `T`, then `@id T' e` typechecks, and Lean
knows that this expression has type `T'` rather than `T`. This can make a
difference for typeclass inference, since `T` and `T'` may have different
typeclass instances on them. `show T' from e` is sugar for an `@id T' e`
expression.
-/
@[inline] def id {α : Sort u} (a : α) : α := a

def allNvar {φ} (h : ∀' φ ∈ Δ) : T ⟹ φ/[&(newVar Δ)] :: Δ → T ⟹ Δ := fun b ↦
  let b : T ⟹ (∀' φ) :: Δ :=
    genelalizeByNewver (by simpa[FVar?] using not_fvar?_newVar h) (fun _ ↦ not_fvar?_newVar) b
  Tait.wk b (by simp[h])

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.eval_iff_of_funEqOn
rag.content:
lemma eval_iff_of_funEqOn [DecidableEq ξ] (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) (h : Function.funEqOn φ.FVar? ε ε') :
    Eval s e ε φ ↔ Eval s e ε' φ := by
  induction φ using Semiformula.rec'
  case hverum => simp
  case hfalsum => simp
  case hrel k r v =>
    simp [eval_rel]; apply iff_of_eq; congr
    funext i
    exact Semiterm.val_eq_of_funEqOn (v i) (fun x hx ↦ h x (fvar?_rel.mpr ⟨i, hx⟩))
  case hnrel k r v =>
    simp [eval_nrel]; apply iff_of_eq; congr
    funext i
    exact Semiterm.val_eq_of_funEqOn (v i) (fun x hx ↦ h x (fvar?_nrel.mpr ⟨i, hx⟩))
  case hand φ ψ ihp ihq =>
    simp; apply and_congr
    · exact ihp fun x hx ↦ h x (by simp [hx])
    · exact ihq fun x hx ↦ h x (by simp [hx])
  case hor φ ψ ihp ihq =>
    simp; apply or_congr
    · exact ihp fun x hx ↦ h x (by simp [hx])
    · exact ihq fun x hx ↦ h x (by simp [hx])
  case hall φ ih =>
    simp; apply forall_congr'; intro x
    exact ih (fun x hx ↦ h _ $ by simp [FVar?]; exact hx)
  case hex φ ih =>
    simp; apply exists_congr; intro x
    exact ih (fun x hx ↦ h _ $ by simp [FVar?]; exact hx)

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.EvalAux
rag.content:
def EvalAux (s : Structure L M) (ε : ξ → M) : ∀ {n}, (Fin n → M) → Semiformula L ξ n → Prop
  | _, _, ⊤        => True
  | _, _, ⊥        => False
  | _, e, rel φ v  => s.rel φ (fun i => Semiterm.val s e ε (v i))
  | _, e, nrel φ v => ¬s.rel φ (fun i => Semiterm.val s e ε (v i))
  | _, e, φ ⋏ ψ    => φ.EvalAux s ε e ∧ ψ.EvalAux s ε e
  | _, e, φ ⋎ ψ    => φ.EvalAux s ε e ∨ ψ.EvalAux s ε e
  | _, e, ∀' φ     => ∀ x : M, (φ.EvalAux s ε (x :> e))
  | _, e, ∃' φ     => ∃ x : M, (φ.EvalAux s ε (x :> e))

rag.content: lemma models_def {φ} : (M ⊧ₘ φ) = ∀ f, Semiformula.Evalf s f φ := rfl

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.EvalAux_neg
rag.content:
@[simp] lemma EvalAux_neg (φ : Semiformula L ξ n) :
    EvalAux s ε e (∼φ) = ¬EvalAux s ε e φ :=
  by induction φ using rec' <;> simp [*, EvalAux, ←neg_eq, or_iff_not_imp_left]

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.eval_toEmpty
rag.content:
lemma eval_toEmpty [DecidableEq ξ] {φ : Semiformula L ξ n} (hp : φ.freeVariables = ∅) : Eval s e f φ ↔ Evalb s e (φ.toEmpty hp) := by
  induction φ using Semiformula.rec'
  case hrel k R v =>
    simp [eval_rel, Semiformula.toEmpty]
    apply iff_of_eq; congr; funext i
    rw [Semiterm.val_toEmpty]
  case hnrel k R v =>
    simp [eval_rel, Semiformula.toEmpty]
    apply iff_of_eq; congr; funext i
    rw [Semiterm.val_toEmpty]
  case hverum => simp
  case hfalsum => simp
  case hand φ ψ ihp ihq =>
    simp [ihp (e := e) (by simp [by simpa [Finset.union_eq_empty] using hp]), ihq (e := e) (by simp [by simpa [Finset.union_eq_empty] using hp])]
  case hor φ ψ ihp ihq =>
    simp [ihp (e := e) (by simp [by simpa [Finset.union_eq_empty] using hp]), ihq (e := e) (by simp [by simpa [Finset.union_eq_empty] using hp])]
  case hall φ ih => simp [fun x ↦ ih (e := (x :> e)) (by simpa using hp)]
  case hex φ ih => simp [fun x ↦ ih (e := (x :> e)) (by simpa using hp)]

rag.content:
lemma eval_nrel {k} {r : L.Rel k} {v} :
    Eval s e ε (nrel r v) ↔ ¬s.rel r (fun i => Semiterm.val s e ε (v i)) := of_eq rfl

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Completeness.Coding
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Order

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

namespace Completeness

open Semiformula Encodable System
variable {L : Language.{u}}
variable {T : Theory L} {Γ : Sequent L}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺[" c:25 "] " Δ₂:80 => Redux T c Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma Redux.antimonotone {c : Code L} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h <;> simp[List.subset_cons_of_subset _ (List.subset_cons_self _ _)]

variable [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Func k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Rel k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Func k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Rel k)]

inductive ReduxNat (T : Theory L) (s : ℕ) : Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | redux {c : Code L} : decode s.unpair.1 = some c → ∀ {Δ₂ Δ₁}, Redux T c Δ₂ Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁
  | refl : decode (α := Code L) s.unpair.1 = none → ∀ Δ, ReduxNat T s Δ Δ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺⟨" s:25 "⟩ " Δ₂:80 => ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma ReduxNat.antimonotone {s : ℕ} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨s⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h; { exact Redux.antimonotone (by assumption) }; { exact List.Subset.refl Δ₂ }

lemma ReduxNat.toRedux {c : Code L} {i} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨(encode c).pair i⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁ := by
  rcases h with (⟨h, r⟩ | ⟨h⟩); { simp at h; simpa[h] using r }; { simp at h }

inductive SearchTreeAux (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : ℕ → Sequent L → Type u
  | zero : SearchTreeAux T Γ 0 Γ
  | succ : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁ → SearchTreeAux T Γ (s + 1) Δ₂

def SearchTree (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) := (s : ℕ) × (Δ : Sequent L) × SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ

namespace SearchTree

abbrev rank (τ : SearchTree T Γ) := τ.1

abbrev seq (τ : SearchTree T Γ) := τ.2.1

inductive Lt (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : SearchTree T Γ → SearchTree T Γ → Prop
  | intro {s} {Δ₂ Δ₁} (a : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁) (r : ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁) : Lt T Γ ⟨s + 1, Δ₂, a.succ r⟩ ⟨s, Δ₁, a⟩

lemma rank_of_lt {τ₁ τ₂ : SearchTree T Γ} (h : Lt T Γ τ₂ τ₁) : τ₂.rank = τ₁.rank + 1 := by
  cases h; simp

lemma seq_of_lt {τ₁ τ₂ : SearchTree T Γ} (h : Lt T Γ τ₂ τ₁) : τ₂.seq ≺⟨τ₁.rank⟩ τ₁.seq := by
  cases h; simp[rank, seq]; assumption

instance : Top (SearchTree T Γ) := ⟨⟨0, Γ, SearchTreeAux.zero⟩⟩

@[simp] lemma rank_top : (⊤ : SearchTree T Γ).rank = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma seq_top : (⊤ : SearchTree T Γ).seq = Γ := rfl

end SearchTree

section WellFounded

variable (wf : WellFounded (SearchTree.Lt T Γ))

noncomputable def SearchTree.recursion {C : SearchTree T Γ → Sort v}
  (τ) (h : ∀ τ₁, (∀ τ₂, SearchTree.Lt T Γ τ₂ τ₁ → C τ₂) → C τ₁) : C τ := by exact?

informal_statement: For every natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p \) such that \( p > n \). Equivalently, there are infinitely many prime numbers.
informal_proof:
First, we fix an arbitrary natural number \( n \).

Next, we consider the number \( (n + 1)! + 1 \), where \( ! \) denotes the factorial function. By the definition of factorial, \( (n + 1)! \) is the product of all positive integers up to \( n + 1 \). Adding 1 to this product gives us \( (n + 1)! + 1 \).

We observe that \( (n + 1)! + 1 \) is greater than or equal to 2, since factorial values are always at least 1, and adding 1 ensures the result is at least 2.

Since \( (n + 1)! + 1 \) is greater than or equal to 2, it must have at least one prime factor \( p \). (This is based on the fundamental theorem of arithmetic, which states that every integer greater than 1 is either a prime itself or can be factored into primes.)

We aim to show that this prime factor \( p \) satisfies \( p > n \). Suppose, for contradiction, that \( p \leq n \). Then, since \( p \) is a prime number dividing \( (n + 1)! \) (because \( p \leq n + 1 \) and hence must be a factor of \( (n + 1)! \) ), it follows that \( p \) also divides the difference between \( (n + 1)! + 1 \) and \( (n + 1)! \), which is 1.

However, the only positive integer that divides 1 is 1 itself. This contradicts the fact that \( p \) is a prime number, and all prime numbers are greater than 1.

This contradiction implies that our assumption \( p \leq n \) is false, and therefore \( p > n \).

Thus, for every natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p \) such that \( p > n \), proving that there are infinitely many prime numbers.

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

lemma val_free (a : M) (t : SyntacticSemiterm L (n + 1)) :
    (Rew.free t).val s e (a :>ₙ ε) = t.val s (e <: a) ε :=
  by simp [val_rew]; congr; exact funext $ Fin.lastCases (by simp) (by simp)

    (Rew.fix t).val s (e <: a) ε = t.val s e (a :>ₙ ε) :=
  by simp [val_rew]; congr <;> simp [Function.comp_def]; exact funext (Nat.cases (by simp) (by simp))

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Rew.eq_bind
rag.content:
lemma eq_bind (ω : Rew L ξ₁ n₁ ξ₂ n₂) : ω = bind (ω ∘ bvar) (ω ∘ fvar) := by
  ext t; induction t ;simp [Rew.func'']; simp [*]

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.eval_rew
rag.content:
lemma eval_rew (ω : Rew L ξ₁ n₁ ξ₂ n₂) (φ : Semiformula L ξ₁ n₁) :
    Eval s e₂ ε₂ (ω ▹ φ) ↔ Eval s (Semiterm.val s e₂ ε₂ ∘ ω ∘ Semiterm.bvar) (Semiterm.val s e₂ ε₂ ∘ ω ∘ Semiterm.fvar) φ := by
  induction φ using rec' generalizing n₂ <;> simp [*, Semiterm.val_rew, eval_rel, eval_nrel, rew_rel, rew_nrel]
  case hall => simp [Function.comp_def]; exact iff_of_eq <| forall_congr fun x ↦ by congr; funext i; cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp
  case hex => simp [Function.comp_def]; exact exists_congr fun x ↦ iff_of_eq $ by congr; funext i; cases i using Fin.cases <;> simp

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.valm_uLift
rag.content:
lemma Semiterm.valm_uLift {e : Fin n → ULift.{v'} M} {ε : ξ → ULift.{v'} M} {t : Semiterm L ξ n} :
    Semiterm.valm (ULift.{v'} M) e ε t = ⟨Semiterm.valm M (fun i ↦ (e i).down) (fun i ↦ (ε i).down) t⟩ := by
  induction t <;> simp [*, Semiterm.val_func]

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.lMap_bind
rag.content:
lemma lMap_bind (b : Fin n₁ → Semiterm L₁ ξ₂ n₂) (e : ξ₁ → Semiterm L₁ ξ₂ n₂) (φ : Semiformula L₁ ξ₁ n₁) :
    lMap Φ (Rew.bind b e ▹ φ) = Rew.bind (Semiterm.lMap Φ ∘ b) (Semiterm.lMap Φ ∘ e) ▹ (lMap Φ φ) := by
  induction φ using rec' generalizing ξ₂ n₂ <;>
  simp [*, rew_rel, rew_nrel, lMap_rel, lMap_nrel, Semiterm.lMap_bind, Rew.q_bind, Matrix.comp_vecCons', Semiterm.lMap_bShift, Function.comp_def]

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.eval_rewrite
rag.content:
lemma eval_rewrite (f : ξ₁ → Semiterm L ξ₂ n) (φ : Semiformula L ξ₁ n) :
    Eval s e ε₂ (Rew.rewrite f ▹ φ) ↔ Eval s e (fun x ↦ (f x).val s e ε₂) φ := by
  simp [eval_rew, Function.comp_def]

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula.eval_rew_q
rag.content:
lemma eval_rew_q {ε₂ : ξ₂ → M} (ω : Rew L ξ₁ n₁ ξ₂ n₂) (φ : Semiformula L ξ₁ (n₁ + 1)) :
    Eval s (x :> e₂) ε₂ (ω.q ▹ φ) ↔
    Eval s
      (x :> Semiterm.val s e₂ ε₂ ∘ ω ∘ Semiterm.bvar)
      (Semiterm.val s e₂ ε₂ ∘ ω ∘ Semiterm.fvar) φ := by
  simp [eval_rew, Function.comp_def]
  apply iff_of_eq; congr 2
  · funext x
    cases x using Fin.cases <;> simp

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.val_rew
rag.content:
lemma val_rew (ω : Rew L μ₁ n₁ μ₂ n₂) (t : Semiterm L μ₁ n₁) :
    (ω t).val s e₂ ε₂ = t.val s (val s e₂ ε₂ ∘ ω ∘ bvar) (val s e₂ ε₂ ∘ ω ∘ fvar) :=
  by induction t <;> simp [*, Rew.func, val_func]

rag.name: LO.FirstOrder.Semiterm.val_rewrite
rag.content:
lemma val_rewrite (f : μ₁ → Semiterm L μ₂ n) (t : Semiterm L μ₁ n) :
    (Rew.rewrite f t).val s e ε₂ = t.val s e (fun x => (f x).val s e ε₂) :=
  by simp [val_rew]; congr

open LO.FirstOrder.Semiformula Encodable LO.FirstOrder.System

variable {L : Language.{u}} {T : Theory L} {Γ : Sequent L} [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Func k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Rel k)]
  [∀ k, Encodable (L.Func k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Rel k)]
informal_statement:
For all first-order logic terms \( t \), the interpretation of \( t \) in the model is equivalent to binding the expression \( e \) with the model structure \( \varepsilon \) to \( t \). Formally:
\[
\text{Model.val}(\Gamma, t) = \text{Rew.bind}(e, \varepsilon, t)
\]
informal_proof:
To prove that for all first-order logic terms \( t \), the interpretation of \( t \) in the model is equivalent to binding the expression \( e \) with the model structure \( \varepsilon \) to \( t \), we use induction on the structure of the term \( t \).

**Case 1: Atomic Term**

If \( t \) is an atomic term, it represents either a variable or a constant. 

- If \( t \) is a variable \( x \), then \( \text{Model.val}(\Gamma, t) \) returns the value assigned to \( x \) by \( \varepsilon \). Similarly, \( \text{Rew.bind}(e, \varepsilon, x) \) would evaluate \( e \) in the context of \( \varepsilon \), which also yields the value assigned to \( x \). Thus, \( \text{Model.val}(\Gamma, t) = \text{Rew.bind}(e, \varepsilon, t) \).

- If \( t \) is a constant symbol \( c \), then \( \text{Model.val}(\Gamma, t) \) is the interpretation of \( c \) in the model. \( \text{Rew.bind}(e, \varepsilon, c) \) would still evaluate to the interpretation of \( c \), as constants are not dependent on bound variables. Hence, \( \text{Model.val}(\Gamma, t) = \text{Rew.bind}(e, \varepsilon, t) \).

**Case 2: Variable**

If \( t \) is a variable \( x \), the behavior is identical to the atomic term case, ensuring that \( \text{Model.val}(\Gamma, t) = \text{Rew.bind}(e, \varepsilon, t) \).

**Case 3: Function Application**

If \( t \) is a function application \( f(t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_n) \), where \( f \) is an \( n \)-ary function symbol, then:

- \( \text{Model.val}(\Gamma, t) \) computes the interpretation of \( f \) using the interpretations of its arguments \( t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_n \) from the model \( \Gamma \).

- \( \text{Rew.bind}(e, \varepsilon, t) \) first evaluates the expression \( e \) in the context of \( \varepsilon \), which provides the interpretation of \( f \) and its arguments. Applying \( \text{Rew.bind} \) would then use these interpretations to compute the final value of \( t \).

Since both \( \text{Model.val} \) and \( \text{Rew.bind} \) follow the same evaluation rules for function applications, it follows that \( \text{Model.val}(\Gamma, t) = \text{Rew.bind}(e, \varepsilon, t) \).

By induction, the statement holds for all first-order logic terms \( t \).

  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :

  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ

  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/

rag.content:
private def deductionAux {Γ : Sequent L} : T ⟹ Γ → T \ {φ} ⟹ ∼(∀∀φ) :: Γ
  | axL Γ R v       => Tait.wkTail <| axL Γ R v
  | verum Γ         => Tait.wkTail <| verum Γ
  | and d₁ d₂       => Tait.rotate₁ <| and (Tait.rotate₁ (deductionAux d₁)) (Tait.rotate₁ (deductionAux d₂))
  | or d            => Tait.rotate₁ <| or (Tait.rotate₂ (deductionAux d))
  | all d           => Tait.rotate₁ <| all (Derivation.cast (Tait.rotate₁ (deductionAux d)) (by simp))
  | ex t d          => Tait.rotate₁ <| ex t <| Tait.rotate₁ (deductionAux d)
  | wk d ss         => wk (deductionAux d) (by simp [List.subset_cons_of_subset _ ss])
  | cut d₁ d₂       => (Tait.rotate₁ <| deductionAux d₁).cut (Tait.rotate₁ <| deductionAux d₂)
  | root (φ := ψ) h => if hq : φ = ψ then Derivation.cast (not_close' φ) (by simp [hq]) else
    have : T \ {φ} ⟹. ψ := root (by simp [h, Ne.symm hq])
    wk this (by simp)

namespace LO

namespace Completeness

open Semiformula Encodable System
variable {L : Language.{u}}
variable {T : Theory L} {Γ : Sequent L}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

lemma Redux.antimonotone {c : Code L} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h <;> simp[List.subset_cons_of_subset _ (List.subset_cons_self _ _)]

variable [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Func k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Rel k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Func k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Rel k)]

inductive ReduxNat (T : Theory L) (s : ℕ) : Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | redux {c : Code L} : decode s.unpair.1 = some c → ∀ {Δ₂ Δ₁}, Redux T c Δ₂ Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁
  | refl : decode (α := Code L) s.unpair.1 = none → ∀ Δ, ReduxNat T s Δ Δ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺⟨" s:25 "⟩ " Δ₂:80 => ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma ReduxNat.antimonotone {s : ℕ} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨s⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h; { exact Redux.antimonotone (by assumption) }; { exact List.Subset.refl Δ₂ }

lemma ReduxNat.toRedux {c : Code L} {i} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨(encode c).pair i⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁ := by
  rcases h with (⟨h, r⟩ | ⟨h⟩); { simp at h; simpa[h] using r }; { simp at h }

  | zero : SearchTreeAux T Γ 0 Γ

lemma rank_of_lt {τ₁ τ₂ : SearchTree T Γ} (h : Lt T Γ τ₂ τ₁) : τ₂.rank = τ₁.rank + 1 := by
  cases h; simp

lemma seq_of_lt {τ₁ τ₂ : SearchTree T Γ} (h : Lt T Γ τ₂ τ₁) : τ₂.seq ≺⟨τ₁.rank⟩ τ₁.seq := by
  cases h; simp[rank, seq]; assumption

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Completeness.Coding

open Semiformula Encodable System
variable {L : Language.{u}}
variable {T : Theory L} {Γ : Sequent L}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

lemma Redux.antimonotone {c : Code L} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h <;> simp[List.subset_cons_of_subset _ (List.subset_cons_self _ _)]

inductive ReduxNat (T : Theory L) (s : ℕ) : Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | redux {c : Code L} : decode s.unpair.1 = some c → ∀ {Δ₂ Δ₁}, Redux T c Δ₂ Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁

lemma ReduxNat.antimonotone {s : ℕ} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨s⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h; { exact Redux.antimonotone (by assumption) }; { exact List.Subset.refl Δ₂ }

  rcases h with (⟨h, r⟩ | ⟨h⟩); { simp at h; simpa[h] using r }; { simp at h }

informal_statement: The model is defined as the set of all syntactic terms in the given language \( L \).
informal_proof: First, we consider the definition of a model as an abbreviation for `SyntacticTerm L`, which represents the set of all terms that can be formed using the language \( L \). Since the model is defined as `SyntacticTerm L`, it serves as a fundamental structure consisting solely of the syntactic components of the language. This means the model includes all possible terms, constants, functions, and quantifiers that can be expressed within \( L \), but it does not yet incorporate any semantic interpretation or domain of discourse. By itself, the model provides the foundational syntax necessary for constructing a complete logical framework, but it remains a purely syntactic entity until an interpretation is applied to it.

variable {L : Language.{u}}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

  cases h <;> simp[List.subset_cons_of_subset _ (List.subset_cons_self _ _)]

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Completeness.Coding
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Order

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

namespace Completeness

open Semiformula Encodable System
variable {L : Language.{u}}
variable {T : Theory L} {Γ : Sequent L}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺[" c:25 "] " Δ₂:80 => Redux T c Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma Redux.antimonotone {c : Code L} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h <;> simp[List.subset_cons_of_subset _ (List.subset_cons_self _ _)]

variable [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Func k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Rel k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Func k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Rel k)]

inductive ReduxNat (T : Theory L) (s : ℕ) : Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | redux {c : Code L} : decode s.unpair.1 = some c → ∀ {Δ₂ Δ₁}, Redux T c Δ₂ Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁
  | refl : decode (α := Code L) s.unpair.1 = none → ∀ Δ, ReduxNat T s Δ Δ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺⟨" s:25 "⟩ " Δ₂:80 => ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma ReduxNat.antimonotone {s : ℕ} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨s⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h; { exact Redux.antimonotone (by assumption) }; { exact List.Subset.refl Δ₂ }

lemma ReduxNat.toRedux {c : Code L} {i} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨(encode c).pair i⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁ := by
  rcases h with (⟨h, r⟩ | ⟨h⟩); { simp at h; simpa[h] using r }; { simp at h }

inductive SearchTreeAux (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : ℕ → Sequent L → Type u
  | zero : SearchTreeAux T Γ 0 Γ
  | succ : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁ → SearchTreeAux T Γ (s + 1) Δ₂

def SearchTree (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) := (s : ℕ) × (Δ : Sequent L) × SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ

@[simp] lemma cast_substs_eq (t : SyntacticTerm L) (φ : S 0) :
    (Rewriting.substitute (ξ := ℕ) φ ![])/[t] = φ := by
  suffices (Rewriting.substitute (ξ := ℕ) φ ![])/[t] = Rew.id ▹ φ by rwa [ReflectiveRewriting.id_app] at this
  simpa [←comp_app, -id_app] using smul_ext' <| by
    ext x <;> simp only [Rew.comp_app, Rew.substs_bvar, Rew.substs_fvar, Rew.id_app]
    exact x.elim0

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Completeness.Coding
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Order

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

namespace Completeness

open Semiformula Encodable System
variable {L : Language.{u}}
variable {T : Theory L} {Γ : Sequent L}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺[" c:25 "] " Δ₂:80 => Redux T c Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma Redux.antimonotone {c : Code L} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h <;> simp[List.subset_cons_of_subset _ (List.subset_cons_self _ _)]

variable [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Func k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Rel k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Func k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Rel k)]

inductive ReduxNat (T : Theory L) (s : ℕ) : Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | redux {c : Code L} : decode s.unpair.1 = some c → ∀ {Δ₂ Δ₁}, Redux T c Δ₂ Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁
  | refl : decode (α := Code L) s.unpair.1 = none → ∀ Δ, ReduxNat T s Δ Δ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺⟨" s:25 "⟩ " Δ₂:80 => ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma ReduxNat.antimonotone {s : ℕ} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨s⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h; { exact Redux.antimonotone (by assumption) }; { exact List.Subset.refl Δ₂ }

lemma ReduxNat.toRedux {c : Code L} {i} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨(encode c).pair i⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁ := by
  rcases h with (⟨h, r⟩ | ⟨h⟩); { simp at h; simpa[h] using r }; { simp at h }

inductive SearchTreeAux (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : ℕ → Sequent L → Type u
  | zero : SearchTreeAux T Γ 0 Γ
  | succ : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁ → SearchTreeAux T Γ (s + 1) Δ₂

def SearchTree (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) := (s : ℕ) × (Δ : Sequent L) × SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ

namespace SearchTree

abbrev rank (τ : SearchTree T Γ) := τ.1

abbrev seq (τ : SearchTree T Γ) := τ.2.1

inductive Lt (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : SearchTree T Γ → SearchTree T Γ → Prop
  | intro {s} {Δ₂ Δ₁} (a : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁) (r : ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁) : Lt T Γ ⟨s + 1, Δ₂, a.succ r⟩ ⟨s, Δ₁, a⟩
annotation:
inductive Lt (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : SearchTree T Γ → SearchTree T Γ → Prop
  | intro {s} {Δ₂ Δ₁} (a : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁) (r : ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁) : Lt T Γ ⟨s + 1, Δ₂, a.succ r⟩ ⟨s, Δ₁, a⟩

informal_statement: For every syntactic semiformula $\phi$ in the theory, there exists a term $t$ such that substituting $t$ into $\phi$ results in a formula that remains within the set of all syntactic semiformulas associated with the theory.
informal_proof: Firstly, we consider an arbitrary syntactic semiformula $\phi$ within the set of all such semiformulas for the given theory. Given that the set of syntactic semiformulas $\Gamma$ is closed under substitution (a property implied by the well-foundedness of the relation under consideration), there must exist at least one term $t$ that can be substituted into $\phi$ without causing the resulting formula to fall outside of $\Gamma$. This follows from the fact that the theory's well-foundedness ensures that such substitutions do not lead to inconsistencies or elements outside the defined structure. Specifically, by applying the `chain_spec'` lemma, we can identify a term $t$ that extends the chain of substitution operations without violating the properties of $\Gamma$. Therefore, we can assert that there exists a term $t$ such that the substitution $\phi/[t]$ remains a member of $\Gamma$. This completes the proof.

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Completeness.Coding
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Order

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

namespace Completeness

open Semiformula Encodable System
variable {L : Language.{u}}
variable {T : Theory L} {Γ : Sequent L}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

inductive ReduxNat (T : Theory L) (s : ℕ) : Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | redux {c : Code L} : decode s.unpair.1 = some c → ∀ {Δ₂ Δ₁}, Redux T c Δ₂ Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁
  | refl : decode (α := Code L) s.unpair.1 = none → ∀ Δ, ReduxNat T s Δ Δ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺⟨" s:25 "⟩ " Δ₂:80 => ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma ReduxNat.antimonotone {s : ℕ} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨s⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h; { exact Redux.antimonotone (by assumption) }; { exact List.Subset.refl Δ₂ }

lemma ReduxNat.toRedux {c : Code L} {i} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨(encode c).pair i⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁ := by
  rcases h with (⟨h, r⟩ | ⟨h⟩); { simp at h; simpa[h] using r }; { simp at h }

inductive SearchTreeAux (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : ℕ → Sequent L → Type u
  | zero : SearchTreeAux T Γ 0 Γ
  | succ : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁ → SearchTreeAux T Γ (s + 1) Δ₂

def SearchTree (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) := (s : ℕ) × (Δ : Sequent L) × SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ

namespace SearchTree

abbrev rank (τ : SearchTree T Γ) := τ.1

abbrev seq (τ : SearchTree T Γ) := τ.2.1

inductive Lt (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : SearchTree T Γ → SearchTree T Γ → Prop
  | intro {s} {Δ₂ Δ₁} (a : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁) (r : ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁) : Lt T Γ ⟨s + 1, Δ₂, a.succ r⟩ ⟨s, Δ₁, a⟩

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Completeness.Coding
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Order

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

namespace Completeness

open Semiformula Encodable System
variable {L : Language.{u}}
variable {T : Theory L} {Γ : Sequent L}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺[" c:25 "] " Δ₂:80 => Redux T c Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma Redux.antimonotone {c : Code L} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h <;> simp[List.subset_cons_of_subset _ (List.subset_cons_self _ _)]

variable [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Func k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Rel k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Func k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Rel k)]

inductive ReduxNat (T : Theory L) (s : ℕ) : Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | redux {c : Code L} : decode s.unpair.1 = some c → ∀ {Δ₂ Δ₁}, Redux T c Δ₂ Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁
  | refl : decode (α := Code L) s.unpair.1 = none → ∀ Δ, ReduxNat T s Δ Δ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺⟨" s:25 "⟩ " Δ₂:80 => ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma ReduxNat.antimonotone {s : ℕ} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨s⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h; { exact Redux.antimonotone (by assumption) }; { exact List.Subset.refl Δ₂ }

lemma ReduxNat.toRedux {c : Code L} {i} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨(encode c).pair i⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁ := by
  rcases h with (⟨h, r⟩ | ⟨h⟩); { simp at h; simpa[h] using r }; { simp at h }

inductive SearchTreeAux (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : ℕ → Sequent L → Type u
  | zero : SearchTreeAux T Γ 0 Γ
  | succ : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁ → SearchTreeAux T Γ (s + 1) Δ₂

def SearchTree (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) := (s : ℕ) × (Δ : Sequent L) × SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ

informal_statement: If there exists a position in a certain structure where the conjunction of two formulas φ and ψ holds, then at least one of these formulas must also hold at that position.
informal_proof:
We start by assuming that there is a position `s` where the conjunction `φ ∧ ψ` holds. This means that both formulas `φ` and `ψ` evaluate to `true` at position `s`. 

From the structure of the proof, we can argue that either `φ` holds at `s` or `ψ` holds at `s`. If both hold, then their conjunction also holds, which is consistent with our assumption. However, if neither held, it would contradict some property related to the well-foundedness or the ordering of the structure. Specifically, the assumption that the structure does not allow for infinite descending chains combined with the presence of the conjunction at position `s` implies that at least one of the individual formulas must also be present at that same position.

Therefore, since both `φ ∧ ψ` and `φ` holding implies `φ` holds, and similarly for `ψ`, we conclude that either `φ` holds or `ψ` holds at position `s`. This satisfies the lemma's requirement that if the conjunction holds, at least one of the formulas must also hold.

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Completeness.Coding
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Order

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

namespace Completeness

open Semiformula Encodable System
variable {L : Language.{u}}
variable {T : Theory L} {Γ : Sequent L}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺[" c:25 "] " Δ₂:80 => Redux T c Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma Redux.antimonotone {c : Code L} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h <;> simp[List.subset_cons_of_subset _ (List.subset_cons_self _ _)]

variable [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Func k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Rel k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Func k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Rel k)]

inductive ReduxNat (T : Theory L) (s : ℕ) : Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | redux {c : Code L} : decode s.unpair.1 = some c → ∀ {Δ₂ Δ₁}, Redux T c Δ₂ Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁
  | refl : decode (α := Code L) s.unpair.1 = none → ∀ Δ, ReduxNat T s Δ Δ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺⟨" s:25 "⟩ " Δ₂:80 => ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma ReduxNat.antimonotone {s : ℕ} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨s⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h; { exact Redux.antimonotone (by assumption) }; { exact List.Subset.refl Δ₂ }

lemma ReduxNat.toRedux {c : Code L} {i} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨(encode c).pair i⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁ := by
  rcases h with (⟨h, r⟩ | ⟨h⟩); { simp at h; simpa[h] using r }; { simp at h }

inductive SearchTreeAux (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : ℕ → Sequent L → Type u
  | zero : SearchTreeAux T Γ 0 Γ
  | succ : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁ → SearchTreeAux T Γ (s + 1) Δ₂

def SearchTree (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) := (s : ℕ) × (Δ : Sequent L) × SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ

namespace SearchTree

abbrev rank (τ : SearchTree T Γ) := τ.1

abbrev seq (τ : SearchTree T Γ) := τ.2.1

inductive Lt (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : SearchTree T Γ → SearchTree T Γ → Prop
  | intro {s} {Δ₂ Δ₁} (a : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁) (r : ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁) : Lt T Γ ⟨s + 1, Δ₂, a.succ r⟩ ⟨s, Δ₁, a⟩

  | intro {s} {Δ₂ Δ₁} (a : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁) (r : ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁) : Lt T Γ ⟨s + 1, Δ₂, a.succ r⟩ ⟨s, Δ₁, a⟩

informal_statement: For a given relation `r` and type `T` with a well-founded order on `T`, if neither `rel r v` nor `nrel r v` is an element of the proposition set `Prop ∖ {True}`, then a contradiction arises. Therefore, at least one of these relations must belong to `Prop ∖ {True}`.
informal_proof:
Assume, for the sake of contradiction, that neither `rel r v` nor `nrel r v` is an element of `Prop ∖ {True}`. This implies that for the given relation and type, the propositions `rel r v` and `nrel r v` are either false or belong to a set where they are not considered true. 

By constructing an appropriate pair or combined structure from these assumptions, we observe that both `rel r v` and `nrel r v` must simultaneously hold within this context, leading to a contradiction due to the well-foundedness of the order on `T` and the encoding (`Code.axL`) which ensures mutual exclusivity of these relations. Specifically, the encoding enforces that these relations cannot coexist without resulting in a logical inconsistency. Hence, our initial assumption is flawed, and consequently, at least one of `rel r v` or `nrel r v` must indeed be an element of `Prop ∖ {True}`.

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

First, we consider an arbitrary chain \( S \) and an element \( s \) within \( S \). Assuming the condition \( \texttt{nwf} \), we proceed to analyze the set \( \texttt{chainSet} \).

By applying the `simp` tactic, we simplify the goal to show that \( \top \) does not belong to \( \texttt{chainSet} \). We introduce an arbitrary element \( h \) from \( \texttt{chainSet} \) and use `chain_monotone` to establish monotonicity within the chain.

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Completeness.Coding
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Order

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

namespace Completeness

open Semiformula Encodable System
variable {L : Language.{u}}
variable {T : Theory L} {Γ : Sequent L}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺[" c:25 "] " Δ₂:80 => Redux T c Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma Redux.antimonotone {c : Code L} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h <;> simp[List.subset_cons_of_subset _ (List.subset_cons_self _ _)]

variable [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Func k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Rel k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Func k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Rel k)]

inductive ReduxNat (T : Theory L) (s : ℕ) : Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | redux {c : Code L} : decode s.unpair.1 = some c → ∀ {Δ₂ Δ₁}, Redux T c Δ₂ Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁
  | refl : decode (α := Code L) s.unpair.1 = none → ∀ Δ, ReduxNat T s Δ Δ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺⟨" s:25 "⟩ " Δ₂:80 => ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma ReduxNat.antimonotone {s : ℕ} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨s⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h; { exact Redux.antimonotone (by assumption) }; { exact List.Subset.refl Δ₂ }

lemma ReduxNat.toRedux {c : Code L} {i} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨(encode c).pair i⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁ := by
  rcases h with (⟨h, r⟩ | ⟨h⟩); { simp at h; simpa[h] using r }; { simp at h }

inductive SearchTreeAux (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : ℕ → Sequent L → Type u
  | zero : SearchTreeAux T Γ 0 Γ
  | succ : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁ → SearchTreeAux T Γ (s + 1) Δ₂

def SearchTree (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) := (s : ℕ) × (Δ : Sequent L) × SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ

namespace SearchTree

abbrev rank (τ : SearchTree T Γ) := by exact?

informal_proof:
First, we consider the properties of the non-well-founded relation `SearchTree.Lt T Γ`. This relation lacks the well-foundedness property, meaning there exists at least one infinite decreasing chain.

Given this property, we apply the lemma `chain_spec` to the code `c` and the position `i`. The lemma `chain_spec` provides a way to compare the encodings of `c` at consecutive positions. Specifically, it shows that incrementing the position `i` results in a smaller encoding.

Finally, by converting the result of applying `chain_spec` into Redux form, we establish the desired inequality between the encodings. This completes the proof that the encoding of `c` decreases when the position `i` is incremented.

variable {L : Language.{u}}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Completeness.Coding
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Order

namespace LO

namespace FirstOrder

namespace Completeness

open Semiformula Encodable System
variable {L : Language.{u}}
variable {T : Theory L} {Γ : Sequent L}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺[" c:25 "] " Δ₂:80 => Redux T c Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma Redux.antimonotone {c : Code L} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h <;> simp[List.subset_cons_of_subset _ (List.subset_cons_self _ _)]

variable [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Func k)] [∀ k, DecidableEq (L.Rel k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Func k)] [∀ k, Encodable (L.Rel k)]

inductive ReduxNat (T : Theory L) (s : ℕ) : Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | redux {c : Code L} : decode s.unpair.1 = some c → ∀ {Δ₂ Δ₁}, Redux T c Δ₂ Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁
  | refl : decode (α := Code L) s.unpair.1 = none → ∀ Δ, ReduxNat T s Δ Δ

local notation:25 Δ₁" ≺⟨" s:25 "⟩ " Δ₂:80 => ReduxNat T s Δ₁ Δ₂

lemma ReduxNat.antimonotone {s : ℕ} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨s⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₁ ⊆ Δ₂ := by
  cases h; { exact Redux.antimonotone (by assumption) }; { exact List.Subset.refl Δ₂ }

lemma ReduxNat.toRedux {c : Code L} {i} {Δ₂ Δ₁ : Sequent L} (h : Δ₂ ≺⟨(encode c).pair i⟩ Δ₁) : Δ₂ ≺[c] Δ₁ := by
  rcases h with (⟨h, r⟩ | ⟨h⟩); { simp at h; simpa[h] using r }; { simp at h }

inductive SearchTreeAux (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) : ℕ → Sequent L → Type u
  | zero : SearchTreeAux T Γ 0 Γ
  | succ : SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ₁ → ReduxNat T s Δ₂ Δ₁ → SearchTreeAux T Γ (s + 1) Δ₂

def SearchTree (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) := (s : ℕ) × (Δ : Sequent L) × SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ
annotation: def SearchTree (T : Theory L) (Γ : Sequent L) := (s : ℕ) × (Δ : Sequent L) × SearchTreeAux T Γ s Δ

lemma subset_of_le {T : ℕ → Set F} (H : Cumulative T)
    {s₁ s₂ : ℕ} (h : s₁ ≤ s₂) : T s₁ ⊆ T s₂ := by
  suffices ∀ s d, T s ⊆ T (s + d) by
    simpa[Nat.add_sub_of_le h] using this s₁ (s₂ - s₁)
  intro s d
  induction' d with d ih
  · simp
  · simpa only [Nat.add_succ, add_zero] using subset_trans ih (H (s + d))

  induction hc with

    exact fun c₁ ⟨t₁, ht₁, (hc₁ : c₁ ∈ t₁)⟩ c₂ ⟨t₂, ht₂, (hc₂ : c₂ ∈ t₂)⟩ hneq =>

        h t₁ ht₁ hc₁ (ht hc₂) hneq

informal_statement: For any natural numbers `s` and `u` where `s` is less than or equal to `u`, the closure of `s` in the context of `SearchTree.Lt T Γ` is a subset of the closure of `u`.
informal_proof:
To prove that for any natural numbers `s` and `u` where `s ≤ u`, the closure of `s` is a subset of the closure of `u` in the context of `SearchTree.Lt T Γ`, we can proceed by induction on the difference between `u` and `s`.

Base Case: When the difference `d = 0`, meaning `s = u`, the closure of `s` is trivially equal to the closure of `u`, so the subset relation holds naturally.

Inductive Step: Assume that for some `d`, `Closure[s] ⊆ Closure[s + d]`. We need to show that `Closure[s] ⊆ Closure[s + (d + 1)]`.

By the inductive hypothesis, every element in `Closure[s]` is also in `Closure[s + d]`. Given that `s ≤ s + 1`, the antimonotonicity property ensures that `Closure[s + d + 1]` is contained within `Closure[s + d]`. Therefore, every element in `Closure[s + d]` is also in `Closure[s + (d + 1)]`.

Thus, by induction, for all natural numbers `d`, `Closure[s] ⊆ Closure[s + d]`. Setting `d = u - s` completes the proof, establishing that `Closure[s] ⊆ Closure[u]` whenever `s ≤ u`.

This proof leverages the inductive structure of natural numbers and the properties of closure and tree ordering to establish the desired subset relation.

import Foundation.FirstOrder.Completeness.Coding

open Semiformula Encodable System
variable {L : Language.{u}}

inductive Redux (T : Theory L) : Code L → Sequent L → Sequent L → Prop
  | axLRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {k} (r : L.Rel k) (v) :
    Semiformula.rel r v ∉ Γ ∨ Semiformula.nrel r v ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.axL r v) Γ Γ
  | verumRefl {Γ : Sequent L} : ⊤ ∉ Γ → Redux T Code.verum Γ Γ
  | and₁      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (φ :: Γ) Γ
  | and₂      {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) (ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | andRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋏ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.and φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | or        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) (φ :: ψ :: Γ) Γ
  | orRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ ψ : SyntacticFormula L} : φ ⋎ ψ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.or φ ψ) Γ Γ
  | all       {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) (φ/[&(newVar Γ)] :: Γ) Γ
  | allRefl   {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} : ∀' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.all φ) Γ Γ
  | ex        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∈ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) (φ/[t] :: Γ) Γ
  | exRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticSemiformula L 1} {t : SyntacticTerm L} :
    ∃' φ ∉ Γ → Redux T (Code.ex φ t) Γ Γ
  | id        {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∈ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) ((∼∀∀φ) :: Γ) Γ
  | idRefl    {Γ : Sequent L} {φ : SyntacticFormula L} (hp : φ ∉ T) : Redux T (Code.id φ) Γ Γ
